fullPassage: In a study of police trainees in the US, Segal found that physical proximity had a stronger effect on attraction, in the short-term, than any other characteristic (such as age, ethnic background and leisure preferences). The trainees were assigned to seats in classrooms and to dormitories on the basis of the first letter of their surname. The closer together in the alphabet the first letters of the surnames of any two individuals were, the more likely they were to be friends. It is worth remembering, however, that physical proximity may increase the likelihood not only of liking someone else, but also of disliking them. A study by Ebbesen and others found that the most-liked others lived close by, but so did the most disliked others. Those who live close by have a greater potential for engaging in behaviours that annoy us (inconsiderate parking, being noisy), which increases the chance that we will dislike them.

Physical proximity had a (A)[stronger / weaker] effect on attraction than any other characteristic. The closer together in the alphabet the surnames were, the (B)[more / less] likely they were to be friends. However, proximity may increase the likelihood not only of liking someone, but also of (C)[disliking / admiring] them.

det.korean: (A) 물리적 근접성이 매력에 '더 강한(stronger)' 영향을 미쳤다, (B) 알파벳이 가까울수록 친구가 될 가능성이 '더 높다(more)', (C) 좋아하는 것뿐만 아니라 '싫어하는 것(disliking)'도 증가한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① stronger — more — disliking: 세 개 모두 원문과 일치한다.
❌ ② stronger — less — admiring: 알파벳이 가까울수록 친구가 더 될 가능성이 높다.
❌ ③ weaker — more — disliking: 근접성의 영향이 더 강하다고 했다.
